newsitem.title: FRANCE: France earmarks 36 bln Ffr for state firms in 96.
newsitem.headline: France earmarks 36 bln Ffr for state firms in 96.

text.p: Some 36 billion francs will be injected into French state-owned companies in 1996, French budget minister Alain Lamassoure said on Thursday.
Of that sum, 8.7 billion francs will come from budgetary sources while the rest will be from privatisation proceeds, he told a finance commission hearing.
Since the start of 1996, more than 12 billion francs have been pumped into publicly owned companies such as Air France and arms maker Giat Industries, he said.
The remaining 24 billion francs would be used toward such ends as financing the state-backed rescue vehicles of bank Credit Lyonnais and recapitalising electronics giant Thomson SA.
Lamassoure reiterated the government's commitment to reduce the 1996 deficit to below 288 billion francs despite lower than expected economic growth.
He said the 1996 deficit would be 35 billion francs lower than the 1995 shortfall.
